cards.html: Before any single tool, it helps to see the whole shape of a good analysis. Every solid piece of analytical work walks the same seven steps, and the best analysts spend most of their time on the first three.

Goal → Question → Metric → Analysis → Insight → Decision → Story, then back to the start: did it work? (close the loop).

StepThe question it answers
1. GoalWhat business outcome are we trying to achieve?
2. QuestionWhat do we need to learn to get there?
3. MetricWhat number tells us the answer?
4. AnalysisPull the data, run the query, build the chart
5. InsightWhat did we actually learn?
6. DecisionWhat should we do differently?
7. StoryPackage the insight so it changes behaviour

Most people jump straight to step 4, the analysis, because that feels like doing something. The best analysts spend most of their time on steps 1 to 3: goal, question and metric. Get those three right and the analysis almost writes itself. Get them wrong and no amount of SQL, and no amount of AI, will save you.

A quick self-check: on your next request, notice how you split your time. If you spent twenty minutes on goal, question and metric and ten minutes on the rest, you walked the loop right. If you jumped straight to pulling data, you did the junior move.

cards.s: Each shortcut has a predictable cost

cards.s: How this track maps onto the loop
cards.html: Each skill in this track trains one part of the loop. Most of them sit at the front, because that is where most wasted analysis starts. Every closed loop gives you a sharper question than the one you started with. So the work builds up over time instead of starting from zero each sprint.

quiz.q: Which step comes right after Metric in the analytics loop?
quiz.why: Goal → Question → Metric → Analysis → Insight → Decision → Story.

quiz.q: Where do the best analysts spend most of their time?
quiz.why: Get the first three steps right and the analysis almost writes itself.

quiz.q: Three teams report three different numbers for the same thing. Which step was skipped?
quiz.why: Without a defined metric, each team computes its own version.

quiz.q: A finding dies in a Slack thread. Which step was skipped?
quiz.why: Skip the decision and nobody acts on the finding.

quiz.q: Jumping straight to pulling data is the fastest way to a useful answer.
quiz.why: Myth. It's the junior move: without goal, question and metric you often answer the wrong thing.
